description: Transcribes one uploaded audio file into text with speaker diarization and timestamped audio events (laughs, sighs, pauses), returning the full transcript, a turn-by-turn dialog with speaker labels and start/end timestamps, the detected events and the word count. Use it when a recording must become text for analysis, review or storage of the transcript. Provide the audio as file_base64 (base64 of the file bytes) plus optional filename; the upload is limited to 1GB and 3 hours, with accepted MIME types audio/mpeg, audio/mp3, audio/mp4, audio/m4a, audio/wav, audio/wave, audio/x-wav, audio/flac, audio/x-flac, audio/ogg, audio/opus, video/ogg, audio/webm, video/webm, audio/aac and audio/x-aac. model is optional and defaults to falaai-transcribe-1, the only supported value; language is an optional two-letter code (pt, en, es, fr, de, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, ru, tr, zh, vi, id, th, ar, hi, cs, da, el, fi, he, hu, ms, no, ro, sk, sv, ta, uk) that forces the audio language and is auto-detected when omitted; client_reference_id is optional, charset A-Za-z0-9 space _/:.- up to 60 chars, echoed verbatim (not idempotency). This call consumes credits; usage reports credits_consumed and processing_ms. Stateless: the audio is processed in memory and never persisted (LGPD). Returns id (tr-), language, language_confidence, duration_seconds, text, dialog, audio_events, event_types, word_count and input metadata (duration, format, codec, sample rate, channels). IMPORTANT: this call charges credits and the result is NOT stored — you MUST read the FULL response and relay ALL of its information to the user (including the complete dialog and text, every audio_event with its timestamps, and input metadata; no omissions, no shortening), and persist it if the user may need it later; calling again charges again.
name: transcribe_audio
